title: Anticipatory Evaluation of Language Models: Predicting LLM Benchmark Scores from Descriptions
abstract: arXiv:2509.20645v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Modern ML research increasingly faces an evaluation bottleneck: building benchmarks and running experiments is costly, slowing iteration. We ask how much can be inferred about evaluation outcomes before experiments, given only a natural-language description of the task and setup. We call this setting anticipatory evaluation. We introduce EVALCAST, a literature-grounded resource of 2,290 description-performance pairs from 1,519 arXiv papers, including a test set of papers published after the model's knowledge cutoff. We evaluate two tasks: predicting absolute performance through regression and comparing benchmark difficulty through pairwise prediction. Experiments with frontier LLMs show that accurate regression remains challenging, while pairwise predictions can recover relative performance ordering under matched settings. translated_title: 语言模型的前瞻性评估：从任务描述预测LLM基准测试分数
translated_abstract: 现代机器学习研究日益面临评估瓶颈：构建基准测试和运行实验成本高昂，拖慢了迭代速度。我们探讨的问题是：在实验之前，仅凭对任务和实验设置的自然语言描述，能够对评估结果推断出多少信息。我们将这一设定称为“前瞻性评估”。我们提出了EVALCAST，一个基于文献构建的资源，包含来自1,519篇arXiv论文的2,290对“描述-性能”数据，其中包括由模型知识截止日期之后发表的论文组成的测试集。我们评估了两项任务：通过回归预测绝对性能，以及通过成对预测比较基准测试的难度。基于前沿LLM的实验表明，精确的回归预测仍然具有挑战性，而成对预测在匹配设置下能够恢复相对性能排序。在截止日期后论文和流式评估上取得相当的表现，说明所观察到的信号并非仅仅……（原文摘要在此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“前瞻性评估”新范式和EVALCAST数据集（2,290对描述-性能数据），证明前沿LLM能够从自然语言任务描述中推断出基准测试的相对难度排序，但精确预测绝对性能分数仍然困难。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the paradigm of "anticipatory evaluation" and the EVALCAST dataset of 2,290 description-performance pairs, demonstrating that frontier LLMs can infer relative benchmark difficulty rankings from natural-language task descriptions, though accurately predicting absolute performance scores remains challenging.
